cells.tense: Right now you're the one keeping this steady, and you know it — not by force, by tending.
cells.ask: Offer one thing you've been holding back to the next person in line, and let them carry it — you get to watch your own care outlive your hands.
cells.core:
Both things that matter are still in your hands, and you haven't picked between them. You tend each one, adding and pulling back as the moment asks, and the steadiness people feel around you is that attention, paid daily. Nothing dramatic, nothing forced — just someone keeping the middle of the thing true, sensing when the mix needs more and when it needs less.

The next step this steadiness is free to take is letting go. When something you've tended reaches its end, releasing it isn't losing it — it's what carrying it was for. Hand one thing off to the next pair of hands, and let the handing-off count as part of the tending. That's the release this earned.
cells.sheetLine: You're the one keeping this steady, and you know it.
cells.verb: tending what grows, with care that doesn't clutch
cells.place: an even keel that's held by constant small adjustments

cells.tense: You're already three steps ahead in your head, bracing for a version of this that hasn't happened yet.
cells.ask: Name one thing that's already finished and let it be finished — you get a satisfaction that doesn't need managing.
cells.core:
Steady and loose is what this looks like when it's right — you hold things lightly, they grow anyway, and the quiet between adjustments is where the settling happens. Your hand isn't on it every hour, and nothing falls apart when you set it down. You read what's needed and let the rest run.

Instead you're tending things that haven't grown yet. Every adjustment is for a future you can't quite see, and you're spending care on loads that may never arrive. You're carrying tomorrow's weight today and calling it keeping up. Go where the work is already done. Name one finished thing and let yourself feel it finished. That settled feeling is what you've been reaching past.
cells.sheetLine: You're tending a future that hasn't asked for you yet.
cells.verb: tending what grows, with care that doesn't clutch
cells.place: an even keel that's held by constant small adjustments

cells.tense: You were tending something once, and you stopped — the door closed behind you and you're still standing there.
cells.ask: Pick up one thing you set down and tend it for a week without asking whether it's worth it — the shine of something you actually finished finds you.
cells.core:
Done steadily, this is growth that doesn't force — you hold space without clutching, the small adjustments return on their own, and what you tend gets to ripen at its own speed.

But you know how to tend things, and you're not doing it. The care that used to move through your hands has gone quiet, and nothing you've tried to force back into place has taken. The knowing is still there; the tending isn't. Tend one small thing and let it finish. Not because it matters, but because finishing is what brings the care back — the shine comes after, not before.
cells.sheetLine: You know how to tend and you've stopped tending.

cells.tense: You're already keeping this steady — adjusting, smoothing, holding — but you talk about it like it's just how things happen to work.
cells.ask: Name one piece of your care that you've been calling upkeep — the weight of what you've carried gets seen, at last, by you.
cells.core:
Held steadily, this is soft hands on something that could be gripped — you let things end when they end, and the quiet tending is the whole of it. You sense when to add, when to subtract, and you do it without making a ceremony of it. Nothing announces itself; the work just gets done.

And you're already the one doing it. Every day you adjust and smooth and hold, and you describe it as just how things work. The care is running; your hand in it goes unnamed. Say the simplest, truest version: this is mine. Claim one piece of what you do, out loud. What you've carried has been real the whole time.
cells.sheetLine: You're already tending this. You just haven't owned it yet.
